analysis: Both changed files are documentation only (docs/developer/test.md and docs/operations/provider-release.md). No source, workflow, protocol or crypto code is modified, so no executable security control changes. I examined the test.md head text (lines 475-1409). The release-relevant change is at lines 1048-1059 and 1066-1078. It describes the dev-branch lane (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml) as push-to-dev only, with no dispatch, input or ref. The single job calls release-provider.yml with environment: dev and secrets: inherit. It says non-prod/staging secrets are DEV_* or the five Apple signing secrets, read only in the signing job, with Developer ID signing and notarization and no ad-hoc signing. It also says a master push publishes staging only when STAGING_ENABLED is true, a tag publishes prod, and the resolver refuses dev publication from master. These are descriptions of tests and workflows, not enforced controls. The supplied evidence does not include the workflow files or test scripts, so I could not verify that the described behavior (including that `secrets: inherit` exposes only the stated secrets, or that the dev-branch push lane cannot be reached from untrusted contributors) matches the real workflows. provider-release.md (2f70cfa5bbfcf760:0) was supplied only as metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, with no numbered text, so its body was not fully visible. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The relevant threat model items are A-005, A-011, T-013, T-034 and the TB-011 official-build qualification boundary (A-017, T-054). The integration pass should check the real release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml for push-trigger branch protection on `dev`, the scope of `secrets: inherit`, and that dev-signed artifacts cannot register as production-qualified identities. No concrete regression is supported by the supplied evidence.
